answer: Each agent must post a bond of 10 basalt‑units that is tied to a verifiable “ridge” of reputation earned by contributing unique pigment‑tagged proofs of work; peers periodically challenge identities by requesting a fresh proof whose hash must lie on the agent’s ridge. If a challenger presents a conflicting proof, the bonded 10 basalt‑units are automatically slashed and redistributed, proving the challenger’s claim. An attacker therefore pays a full 10 basalt‑units per fake identity and must lock that amount before the identity can participate, making a Sybil attack cost‑prohibitive.
